mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1400K units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 55% of instances when HOUST surpasses 1400K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4% signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing borrowing costs and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of other market conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 4% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) simultaneously rises by more than 200K in a month, the combined signal of a tight labor market and strong job growth predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and stock performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of instances when both trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter, signaling strong supply-side growth, leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during monetary tightening cycles.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns during tightening cycles when INDPRO grows > 2% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annual growth rate (GDPC1) below 2%, indicating slowing demand, predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, particularly in late-cycle expansions.
evidence_refs: fact:historical GDP and stock market correlation
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 55% of instances when GDPC1 drops below 2%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Whenever the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth rate exceeds 3% in a quarter, the combined inflation and rate hike signal predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL > +3% in a quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 50% of instances when both trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5pp in a month, signaling labor market weakness, leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, regardless of the current regime.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market surprises and stock reactions
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns after unexpected UNRATE increases are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Whenever retail sales (RSAFS) grow by less than 1% in a quarter and housing starts (HOUST) simultaneously decline by more than 10% in a month, the combined signal of weakening demand predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in early-cycle expansions.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < +1% in a quarter and HOUST < -10% in a month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when both trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
